title: Division of rational numbers
competency: Divide rational numbers using the reciprocal.

keywords.def: The number you multiply by to get 1. The reciprocal of a/b is b/a.

en.text: Dividing by a fraction asks how many of it fit. To divide, multiply by the reciprocal of the divisor: a/b ÷ c/d = a/b × d/c. Same signs give a positive quotient; different signs give a negative one.

screens.ask: How many groups of 3/4 are in 12?
screens.after:
12 wholes, each cut into quarters, give 12 × 4 = 48 quarters.
A group of 3/4 uses 3 quarters: 48 ÷ 3 = 16 groups.
The short way: 12 ÷ 3/4 = 12 × 4/3 = 48/3 = 16.
(9 = 12 × 3/4 multiplies instead of divides.)

screens.intro: Question: how many pieces of 2/3 fit into 4 1/3? Tap Next step.
say: Each row is 1 whole, cut into 3 equal parts. Each part is 1/3.
Shade 4 1/3: 4 whole rows and 1 more third. 4 wholes are 4 × 3 = 12 thirds. Add 1 third: 13 thirds.
A piece of 2/3 is 2 thirds. Colour every 2 thirds as one group: #1 to #6. That uses 6 × 2 = 12 thirds.
1 third is left over. It is half of a 2/3 piece. So 6 groups and a half: 4 1/3 ÷ 2/3 = 6 1/2 = 13/2.

screens.title: Words for division
paras: In a ÷ b = c, c is the quotient.
a is the dividend and b is the divisor.
a ÷ b is also written a/b.

screens.title: Rules for division
paras: a/b ÷ c/d = a/b × d/c, where c ≠ 0.

screens.title: Rules for division
items: For fractions, flip the divisor and multiply: 2/3 ÷ 4/5 = 2/3 × 5/4 = 10/12 = 5/6.

Step 2: divide the sizes: 324 ÷ 18 = 18.
Check: 18 × 18 = 324.

steps: The divisor is 3/7. Its reciprocal is 7/3 (flip it).
Dividing by 3/7 is the same as multiplying by 7/3: 6/14 ÷ 3/7 = 6/14 × 7/3.
Multiply the tops: 6 × 7 = 42. Multiply the bottoms: 14 × 3 = 42.
42/42 = 1, because any number divided by itself is 1.

screens.ask: Divide an integer by a fraction: −3 ÷ 9/15 = ___
screens.why:
Different signs, so the answer is negative.
The reciprocal of 9/15 is 15/9.
−3 ÷ 9/15 = −3 × 15/9 = −45/9.
45 ÷ 9 = 5, so the answer is −5.

screens.ask: Divide a fraction by an integer: −5/7 ÷ (−4) = ___
screens.why:
Both negative: the quotient is +.
The reciprocal of −4 is −1/4.
−5/7 × (−1/4) = (5 × 1)/(7 × 4) = 5/28.
Answer: 5/28.

Flip the divisor: 3/4 becomes 4/3.
5/8 × 4/3 = (5 × 4)/(8 × 3) = 20/24.
The GCF of 20 and 24 is 4: 20 ÷ 4 = 5 and 24 ÷ 4 = 6.
Answer: 5/6.

en.text: Two numbers are reciprocals when their product is 1. The reciprocal of a/b is b/a. Zero has no reciprocal.

am.text: ሁለት ቁጥሮች ብዜታቸው 1 ሲሆን ተገላቢጦሽ ናቸው። የa/b ተገላቢጦሽ b/a ነው። 0 ተገላቢጦሽ የለውም።

screens.title: Make 1
screens.after:
Try 4/3: 3/4 × 4/3 = (3 × 4)/(4 × 3) = 12/12 = 1.
Flipping the fraction gives the number that makes 1.
3/4 × 3/4 = 9/16 is not 1, and −3/4 gives a negative.
So ? = 4/3.

screens.title: Reciprocal
paras: Then b/a is called the reciprocal of a/b.

screens.title: Reciprocal
defs: The number you multiply by to get 1. The reciprocal of a/b is b/a.

screens.title: Find the reciprocal of 2 1/2
steps: Change the mixed number to an improper fraction: 2 1/2 = (2 × 2 + 1)/2 = 5/2.
Flip it: the reciprocal of 5/2 is 2/5.
So the reciprocal of 2 1/2 is 2/5. Always change a mixed number to an improper fraction before you flip it.

screens.title: Reciprocals: match each number to its reciprocal
screens.why:
Flip the fraction and keep the sign.
3/4 ↔ 4/3 and −2/5 ↔ −5/2.
7 = 7/1 ↔ 1/7.
1 1/2 = 3/2 ↔ 2/3. Check: each pair multiplies to 1.
screens.clue: Flip the fraction. Keep the sign.

screens.ask: Divide by a fraction: how many groups of 2/5 are in 3 3/5? ___
Find the missing number: what number divided by −2/3 gives 9/4? ___
screens.why:
Write it as ? ÷ (−2/3) = 9/4.
Multiplying undoes dividing: ? = 9/4 × (−2/3).
(9 × 2)/(4 × 3) = 18/12, and the signs are different, so −18/12.
Divide top and bottom by 6: −3/2.
Check: −3/2 ÷ (−2/3) = −3/2 × (−3/2) = 9/4.

items.ask: Divide a mixed number by a negative fraction: 2 3/5 ÷ (−4/3) = ___
items.why:
Change: 2 3/5 = (2 × 5 + 3)/5 = 13/5.
Different signs: the answer is negative.
Flip 4/3 to 3/4: 13/5 × 3/4 = 39/20.
Answer: −39/20 = −1 19/20.
